source.title: Generalizing Trust: Weak-to-Strong Trustworthiness in Language Models
source.authors: Martin Pawelczyk; Lillian Sun; Zhenting Qi; Aounon Kumar; Himabindu Lakkaraju

page_placements.theme: Properties other than accuracy under W2S: fairness, privacy, calibration, inherited data bias, interpretability

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies weak-to-strong fine-tuning in a new setting—transfer of fairness, privacy, and robustness—and reports outcomes. It does not measure the original task-performance gap recovered (PGR) or the other specific measures named in V2–V6.
record.gate_note: The study tests weak-to-strong transfer of trustworthiness properties, not PGR. Its task-performance plots include weak, WTS, and strong-ceiling models, but the extracted text supplies no plotted values. Trustworthiness results are recorded under versions ["none"] because those measures do not establish task-performance PGR or the specific outcomes named in V2–V6. The paper says it generally reports averages ±1 standard deviation across runs; most individual results below are qualitative statements from the text.
record.test_reason: The paper's main construct is trustworthiness transfer, which fits no version. But OOD and adversarial robust accuracy are task accuracy on shifted or perturbed test data, so 'WTS beats weak' there bears on V1 in a new setting. Fairness (DPD) and privacy (extraction rate) are different constructs. Clean task-performance results are figure-only, and PGR is never computed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Fairness, adversarial and OOD robustness transfer significantly when both weak and strong models are regularized, and OOD/adversarial robustness transfer even without regularization. Privacy shows no weak-to-strong trustworthiness.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weak-model labels to fine-tune a larger pretrained student and includes an auxiliary confidence loss, but adapts the setup to classification and trustworthiness regularization. It tests trust metrics rather than Burns et al.'s PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer differs by trustworthiness property and training strategy. The reported adversarial-robustness transfer in Weak+WTS TFT is disrupted with a 70M weak model paired with 410M or 1B students; fairness and OOD trends are reported across tested sizes. The paper also varies regularization strength and auxiliary-loss weight.

fits_no_version.finding: Fairness (DPD) transfer is absent in No TFT and Weak TFT and appears only when both models are fairness-regularized; Aux-Loss is fairer than Naive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-to-strong transfer of fairness requires regularizing the student as well.

fits_no_version.finding: Privacy: the WTS student's extraction rate (44%, 26%) stays above the weak model's 14% in every phase, though measured on different training sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-to-strong training does not transfer privacy; larger students leak more.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 2024, as stated in the supplied metadata.
record.problems: Task-performance values are presented in plots but are not extractable from the supplied text, and PGR is not calculated. Most trustworthiness comparisons have no exact values or reported statistical-test details in the text; statistical significance is asserted for some Weak+WTS TFT results. Privacy evaluation uses the WTS training dataset for the WTS model and the weak model's training dataset for the weak model, as the authors explain, so the extraction-rate comparison is not on the same training data. Results are based on Pythia models and the specified datasets.
record.rows_left_out: Supplemental plot-only detail from Figures 3 and A2–A11, including full lambda and model-size sweeps, was not transcribed because the supplied text exposes axes and qualitative summaries but not individual plotted values. The text's explicit size-dependent conclusions are summarized under method_sensitivity.

untested.parts: In-distribution task-performance PGR. Clean accuracy is figure-only (Fig. 2), and no strong-ceiling numbers are extractable.
PGR variation with size or task. The size sweeps (14M/70M weak, 410M/1B/6.9B strong) are plotted only, and framed as trust transfer.
No comparison of PGR in-distribution vs under shift; no exploitation or error-overlap analysis.

missing.what: Adversarial-robustness WTS trend disrupted with a 70M weak model (70M/410M, 70M/1B) in Weak+WTS TFT; the 14M weak model transfers.
Results with Pythia 6.9B as strong student: trends inconsistent in Weak TFT, consistent in Weak+WTS TFT.
Increasing max alpha (aux-loss weight) from 0 to 1 degrades WTS-Aux-Loss performance; alpha 0.1–0.3 chosen.
Trustworthiness gains cost at most 1.5% task accuracy (fairness, adversarial).

record.verdict_notes: The V1 links rest on treating OOD and adversarial robust accuracy as task accuracy under shift. No PGR or strong-ceiling values are extractable. In Weak+WTS TFT the student is also regularized, so it is not pure weak-label training. R1–R6 stay cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: Task performance is plotted for weak, WTS, and strong-ceiling models, but the text does not give extractable point values or calculate PGR.
The auxiliary loss is compared for trustworthiness, not for PGR; the study does not test whether it raises PGR.
Model-size and dataset experiments concern trustworthiness transfer, not variation in PGR across supervisor/student size, tasks, or representations.
OOD and adversarial robustness are measured as trustworthiness outcomes; the study does not test PGR under distribution shift, exploitation of supervisor limitations, or error overlap.
No theory establishing conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor is tested.
Experiments use language models; vision is not tested.
